utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, the affirmation you made still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may even be that I don't need to remind you of that anymore after today. Let us see. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, witness, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me ask you, among the documents you reviewed when preparing your report, could you answer whether you had learned that the NLA had military barracks?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. And I think I indicated clearly that they didn't have any barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, in page 49 of the unofficial transcript, you stated that you have seen -- I apologise, 48th page. You stated that you had seen an order issued by Ali Ahmeti quoting some of the regulations that we reviewed yesterday. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at 65 ter 212, R062-6938.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that this document? Do you see it in front of you on the display?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, sir. I have to check the ERN number. Yes, I think this is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see whether this document is referring to some regulations, in the upper part?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. If you read the very first paragraph you will see the following: "On the basis of past experience, and to reorganise the National Liberation Army, thereby applying more concrete measures and activities in a uniform manner, I hereby order as follows." And I think the cover page of this document also has the type written signature of Ali Ahmeti. It is typed-signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But is it correct that it does not refer to any regulation, no rules?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the very next line under number 1, says: "Lodgings and regulations."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But when issuing the order, has he invoked any document. As far as I understand this text, Mr. Ali Ahmeti has issued the following orders. Issuing those orders he is not invoking, referring to any regulation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you really mean, sir. Well, it really depends on the type of the document. It really depends on the type of the regulation. I mean, there is not really an express requirement there each specific case to refer to any particular regulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you testified yesterday that in this document he referred to some regulation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps this is misunderstanding. But I think when we were discussing this issue yesterday, I said that I saw a document signed by Mr. Ali Ahmeti. This is the document I was referring to, and this is in fact the order. I think we were discussing orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see a date on this document, the date when it was issued?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe we could go to the cover page. But I don't think it probably has the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So are you saying that there is no date on this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let me ask you once again: Have you seen an order referring to the regulations that we reviewed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you mean, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When working on your report, have you seen any order referring to the rules that we reviewed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Referring, you mean, directly -- referring in sense of mentioning them?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that's the order was issued on the basis of those regulations.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have -- I have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you indicate which order was that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, this is 65 ter 159, the map with the brief explanatory note which is entitled as: Concept of Operations. And if you read carefully this note, particularly paragraph referring to raising the brigades it would read as -- if I recall correctly, I don't have the document in front of me, but I can pull it out, it says: To continue raising brigades in accordance with established formation. Which clearly indicates to me that these brigades were raised on the basis of the formations, that is those documents, which we had previously discussed, related to brigade and battalion formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. We will review that document a bit later. But this order that you see now in front of you, is it correct that it refers to barracks. It is dealing with barracks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this entire document - and this is in fact, I think, a quite lengthy document - essentially deals with issue of internal regulations, which would include a wide variety of various issues pertaining to the daily routines and everyday life regulations in the army, including the barracks, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But at any rate, the first page, the one that you see in front of you, contains provisions on lodging, and it details the barracks, the premises within the barracks. Then the following three pages -- I apologise. The following five pages deal with that issue?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this document is a part, as I mentioned of a larger document well, if these are the pages which have been translated, perhaps, I think there is, in fact, a number of pages that have been translated at a later stage. Maybe the translation was a little bit late, but I'm pretty certain that this is fact a part of a larger document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I will go back to the issues that we ended with yesterday. We spoke about the territory under the control of NLA. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that it was predominantly villages that were under the NLA control. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really think I said that. What I said that -- according to the documents which I reviewed, and specifically the report of the Ministry of Interior for 2001, the NLA occupied about 20 per cent of the Macedonia territory. Predominantly north and west of the country. And many of the villages, of course, were occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you testified yesterday that the NLA had no city under its control. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that the NLA really controlled, in full, any city, but it is equally clear from the documents that the city of Kumanovo was in fact very close, very close, to being controlled by the NLA. In fact, there was almost street-fighting going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But can you agree with me now that actually the NLA had under its control just villages.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were those villages populated by ethnic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the NLA enjoyed the support of the Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the view which is correct. I think that the NLA indeed had pretty strong support of the local Albanian population, and, in fact, raising an army of about 8.000 men without such support would be simply an impossible and a hopeless undertaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your opinion, ONA enjoyed the support of the political parties of the Albanians as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not specifically looking in this aspect of the conflict, since the political aspect of the conflict is pretty remote from the original goals which I set in my report, but it would appear to me that there was a great deal of sympathy for the NLA on the part of the ethnic Albanian parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It was the PDP and the DPA those are the Macedonian abbreviations of the political parties of Albanians that existed in Macedonia in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the democratic party of Albanians and democratic party of prosperity, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I was referring to those, thank you. When you are saying that the villages were under the NLA control, do you thereby mean control of a military aspect?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at the very basic level, the control or village would mean, in fact, that there was no presence of the Macedonian security forces there, and there was no presence of the Macedonian authorities, government authorities there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And what about the presence of the local authorities, the elected local officials that were elected in the -- in 2000?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not know, obviously. I could not really look into the issue of presence of local authorities in each and every specific village. But coming back again to the issue of the territorial control, I would say that a lot of sources suggest that numerous villages, perhaps running into hundreds, were in fact under NLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the political control of the villages belong to the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, I did not really look into the political aspect of this conflict. This is an entirely different matter and would require an entirely different methodology and entirely different type of analysis. This is political analysis which would have to deal with the political problems of various political parties. The fundamental political issues, the popular support, analysis of the elections, and so on and so forth. But this was not my purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But considering that you testified a moment ago that the NLA enjoyed the support of both ethnic Albanian population as well as the parties PDP and DPA, can it be inferred that the PDP and DPA held the political authority over the Albanian villages?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is something that really needs more analysis, I think. And of course it is really impossible for me to make a sweeping statement like this. I simply cannot tell you whether this is the case or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you as a military analyst now this: Is it justified from a military aspect to conquer a village that is under the control of people who are supporting you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I do not really understand what you mean. It seems that you are indicating some moral aspects of internal politics in Macedonia, but I don't really think it has something to do with military aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you as a military expert because you are a military analyst. Is there a justification from the military aspect to conquer, to take over the village that is under the control of the people who are your supporters.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all I do not quite understand what you mean by "conquer." If you mean to occupy or as to place it under control, I think that in military terms there are numerous instances in the history of warfare when, actually, the powers in times of a conflict were transferred or taken over from civilian by military authorities. For example, the history of war in Bosnia, for that matter, is just full of such instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. When preparing the part of your report when you are alleging which per cent of the Republic of Macedonia was under the NLA control, you are referring to the instruction and the map received from your sources, ethnic Albanians, as you call them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, in making this estimate, I relied on a number of sources, including the Macedonian government source, which I think even more illustrative in this sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But my question is: Did you quote that source? I was reading your report and I know what other sources that you were quoting from, so I'm asking you now about this specific one.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one? You mean the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The instruction on the map received from sources ethnic Albanians.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the concept of operations which was signed by Ali Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P487, please, which has been admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is the map that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I used this map, along with other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the map be closed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You support the opinion that this map is a truthful one and reflects the situation in Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a little bit of an exaggeration. What I'm suggesting is that my analysis and the numbers, in terms of percentage, which I quote in my report, is based on a number of sources. I didn't really say in my report that I absolutely trust this map. And, in fact, in any warfare, the situation regarding the control of territory, including control of certain villages, for example, could be due to the ongoing operations extremely volatile. There are some situations, for example, that, say, a village which was considered to be in the hands of the friendly forces only a few hours ago would, in fact, be taken over by the opposing forces just in the last few hours. Well, at least for this reason I cannot really trust this map completely, but I would say that by and large, essentially I tend to agree that this map represents the true situation on the ground at least as far as the main geographic areas of Macedonia are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown exhibit P466, page 48 in the English version, and page 53 in the Macedonian version. This is paragraph 165. I think we should scroll backwards. We should go three pages back, I think. Could the English version be turned three pages back so we can see paragraph 165.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see -- you now see paragraph 165 of your report. It says: "The analysis of the chronology of the conflict suggests that the NLA operations in July and August 2001 were conducted along the lines of the directive. Despite the fact that not every objective set out in the directive was actually carried out between the time the directive was apparently released and the end of the conflict the NLA made significant gains pushing south from Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo." So in this paragraph you refer to a directive and your conclusion is that the NLA succeeded in gaining huge benefits, pushing south from Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand what you mean by "huge benefits," sir. What I'm say something that there are numerous reports suggesting that in June, July, and August 2001 the NLA was still on the offensive and was in fact occupying more and more territories. Of course, the fighting was concentrated mainly in the area of Tetovo, both north and south of Tetovo, and also south-east from Kumanovo. On --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you claim that the NLA made significant gains pushing south from Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo. That means that the NLA managed to go south of Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo. Have I understood it well?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could specify this, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Please answer with yes or no, whether I have understood it well.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, NLA was pushing south of Tetovo. And I think by August, mid-August in fact, there were many villages which were put under control along the road between Tetovo and Jezince, as well as some villages south of Tetovo, particularly in the area of Marvovo, Marvovo lake, which is south of Tetovo as well as some villages in the area of Gostivar which is again south of Tetovo, and the NLA was also pushing in south-west and south-east of Kumanovo. I think there was a lot of fighting both in south-west and south-east of Kumanovo, which is obvious from a number of documents, but I think the NLA probably did not really succeed in pushing very hard towards Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But they managed to take over territories east of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: East of Kumanovo, yes. Mostly Skopska Crna Gora area. Sorry, not east, west. Skopska Crna Gora area is west of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But in your report you say south-east from Kumanovo. Am I seeing it right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says south-east, yes. But actually it could be south-east, it also could be south-west. General direction was south.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P487.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters' intervention, the exhibit number is P487.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could -- do you recognise this map. This is the directive. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And based on this directive, you wrote paragraph 165, that you -- that I asked you about before and you referred to it, right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the upper part of the map be enlarged, please. Could you enlarge it a little bit more? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the city of Kumanovo here?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you put the number 1 next to the city of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It's not visible. It is not visible again. Could you put number 1 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have underlined the name of Kumanovo on this map and also put a dot here. It's number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Could you please mark with X what part south-east of Kumanovo was occupied by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the NLA penetrated in.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: South-east of Kumanovo. Well, you can see this arrow here. I mark it as number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is the north.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's north, but the direction is south. To be more precise, the direction is south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your report you say that the NLA penetrated south from Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo. Could you indicate the territory south-east of Kumanovo where NLA penetrated?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think this is something I could do on this map because apparently even a small gain of a territory would require a more accurate map than this one, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you claimed that this is a military map used by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the map which was used by the NLA, that's right. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you claimed that this map was made by a professional and it is a very accurate one.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to be made on the professional basis, at least there are military symbols which are professional military symbols on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I ask you once again: Could you then mark where is south-east from Kumanovo and just to mark it with a line. Just take Kumanovo as a reference and then draw a line where south-east is.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think what I mentioned in my report was that in fact NLA was pushing south from Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo. And if you look again at the area around Kumanovo, you will see that there is an arrow which I marked as number 2, which indeed originates from the area close to the border, north of Kumanovo and pointed in direction of south-east of Kumanovo. I don't really think there is any contradiction in my report in this sense. If you are specifically referring which particular gains were made in this particular area, as I mentioned previously, for this reason we have to use another map. But I would imagine that some gains in this area were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that territories south-east from Kumanovo were occupied. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I said there were gains made, probably made in the area south-east of Kumanovo. But also south-west. If you see this area here, in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm not interested about south-west, Witness. Could you mark south-east on the map. Do you want me to read paragraph 165 of your report once again?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you wish, sir, but I think I already answered your question, saying that they were pushing south-east and south-west of Kumanovo. And, again, if you really want me to show any particular gains that apparently were made, or in this area, I simply cannot do it because this is not entirely the appropriate map for this purpose. And, secondly, I don't really think that I have extremely specific knowledge of any locations which had been taken over by the NLA in this particular area. It really requires very specific knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will read paragraph 165 once again. "The analysis of the chronology of the conflict suggests that the operations of the NLA in July and August 2001 were laid in accordance with the directive. Beside the fact that all the goals set forth in the past were not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down. It is impossible to interpret in this pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The NLA managed to gain significant benefit, to make significant gains, pushing south from Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo. I kindly ask you to mark the south-east part from Kumanovo with an arrow, the direction south-east from Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I think I already marked the direction from north to south-east, of Kumanovo, but I'm afraid are you misinterpreting or misreading my sentence. What I said in the sentence was that NLA indeed made big territorial gains, and I also said in this sentence that the NLA was pushing south from Tetovo and south-east from Kumanovo. But I don't think that this sentence should read as territorial gains were made only in Kumanovo area. In fact, I was referring more to those gains made in the area of Tetovo. And if you scroll this map a little bit, I show you what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you now saying something that is conflicting with paragraph 165 of your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on how you really read it, sir. And also depends on how you really understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I am reading it as written. And can I see, and I can read here that the NLA made significant gains, pushing south from -- south-east from Kumanovo. Could you just mark south-east of Kumanovo with an arrow, just that the area south-east from Kumanovo, where is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, I think we all know where the south-east direction is, whether it is from Kumanovo or anywhere else. We're going to confuse the map if we just mark a direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Very well. Could this map be tendered in evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before that happens, the witness also completed the enclosure of a large area to the west and a little north of Kumanovo and north of Skopje. Should that be numbered, because he did refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since he already marked it, he can mark the arrow with the number 3 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreters were not able to hear the last part of the sentence due to some background -- some loud background noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that the transcript reflects enough that the area I was referring to is now numbered 3 and that was an area that the witness mentioned and you said well, that is not essentially -- you said that is not the one that I'm interested in. Let's go to the south-east of Kumanovo. Very well. This map, as marked, will now be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D76, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 65 ter number 388. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you read what is written down on the map?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It has been prepared by the witness, Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ali Ahmeti is the person who could give most accurate and most precise information about which territories were under NLA control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really would not venture this kind of statement. Well, I think that perhaps from the military point of view his Chief of Staff was involved in these actions and operations on the daily basis, probably have more intimate knowledge as what was happening on the grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ali Ahmeti was the commander in chief of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back to the map, and could we please zoom in on the top section where Kumanovo is. That would be towards the middle of the map where the word Skopje is written. Could we move back, yes, it is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You see here Tetovo as well. Isn't it so? To the left-hand side of the map.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move the -- scroll down a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see here the Mavrovo lake? It is on the left-hand side, south-west from Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It is written Mavrovo there.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Referred to my map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I don't want to you to refer to your map; I just want you to look at this map, since this is the exhibit that we are reviewing now.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see Mavrovo lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me there are red circles on the map marking the places, settlements under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really think that I could really basis my analysis of the territorial control exclusively on there map. May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry for the interruption, Your Honour, and it may be my poor eyesight on a Friday morning, simply I cannot see the word Mavrovo on this map, and I'm wondering whether perhaps my colleague or the witness can indicate to us where it is. Ah, okay, now I can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you were interrupted, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's perfectly all right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the Mavrovo lake with the number 1?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here Mavrovo lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you testified previously that, as it is written in paragraph 165, the NLA managed to occupy villages to the south of Tetovo, also near Mavrovo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you allow me, Mr. Apostolski, I would also like to say that for instance the village of Pirok was under NLA control the village of Vrapciste seemed under NLA control. The whole smaller villages along this side of the road were under NLA control. The villages all in this area were under NLA control. If you could go a little bit up, I would say also a lot of smaller villages which are not really on this map in this area were under NLA control. If you go down south and west, I could show you more villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And Ali Ahmeti didn't know that Pirok, and Vrapciste were under his control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he knew it or not, I cannot really tell it for him. But as I mentioned previously my analysis was based not entirely on this particular exhibit, as you would imagine, because, again that would be very irresponsible and unprofessional. My analysis was based on a broad variety of sources which included both Macedonian and sources from within the NLA. Well, therefore, I cannot really say whether Mr. Ali Ahmeti was right or wrong in this particular regard. I only can say that apparently, as is obvious from many other sources, the territorial control the NLA extended far beyond those villages which are marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When preparing your report, did you have access to this map?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you quote from this map anywhere in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not quote Mr. Ali Ahmeti's statement at all, for the reasons I already mentioned on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could the area that you encircled to the north of Skopje be marked with number 1? No, I apologise, number 2, because number 1 was used for the Mavrovo lake.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please explain what is it that you have marked here, what does this area mean?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, this is the area which is north of Skopje. Part of this area is the so-called Skopska Crna Gora, part of this area is the so-called Kumanovo area, and at least a number of villages in this area were in fact under NLA control. If you allow me to be more specific, sir, I'm prepared to give you a list of those villages just to avoid many misunderstanding and not to waste time. If you give me one second --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, I have read all those from your report, which villages were under the NLA control. But did you use the number 2 to mark an area that was under the NLA control in 2001, towards the end of the conflict, in August?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a completely different question, Mr. Apostolski. I think you were talking about the villages which were under NLA control without any specific reference, well, as to the end of the conflict. I'm afraid you're asking me something else now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were the areas under the NLA control compact or was it control over the villages only?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were the areas that you assert were under the NLA control one compact area, meaning that the entire area was under the control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid there is some misunderstanding here, Mr. Apostolski. What I said in my report was that about 20 per cent of the entire Macedonian territory was under the NLA control. Now you are asking me whether this was a compact area. 20 per cent of an entirety territory, well, this is quite a large area, and I'm not sure if this could be described as compact or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were those 20 per cent of the territory connected?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously on a number of occasions, there are several fronts which were opened in the country during the conflict. In fact. If you read Macedonian military documents, especially the Ministry of Defence intelligence summaries, they speak mostly of three, what they call, crisis areas. These were Kumanovo, Skopje and Tetovo. And if you want me to generalise them we can say that if we are talking about these three areas specifically without mentioning Gostivar and Debar well, the entire area would be quite huge and would actually take a lot of territory here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My question was: Were those territories connected between themselves.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could give you perhaps a descriptive answer somehow. In fact the NLA was indeed apparently making effort to connect all those fronts. For example --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Wait a moment. I do not want you to mark this on this document. We will go back to this because otherwise I would not have been able to tendered it in evidence. Do not mark here. One more question about the map that you have in front of you. Do you see to the south or south-east of Kumanovo that Mr. Ali Ahmeti has marked villages under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But for example --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Umin Dol apparently was under NLA control, if I'm not mistaken, which is south of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is to the south-west of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I seek to tender this map in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, I don't want us to be confused by the evidence about this map if we later need to turn to it. I may well have misunderstood the witness, but I understood him to commence to mark areas in which he said villages were under the control of the NLA, and he seems to have circled or enclosed roughly three areas. He also said that if the map was scrolled further to the north or further to the south and west, he could mark more areas, if I understood him correctly. Now is this your understanding or have I got it wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, then I would remove this document and go back to the full map. So could we please display 548 -- no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You don't want to use this at all or preserve this at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this into evidence, and I wish to go back to the same map; and I would like to ask the witness then to mark at the entire map which were the territories under the NLA control, since I used this map just to mark the territory south of Tetovo and to show the area of Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We can receive this map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 2D77, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now you want this map to be displayed again but in a more full view.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This map or another map?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like this map to be displayed again, the 65 ter 388, the original one. Could we please zoom it in. Could we zoom out once only. And scroll towards the right-hand side. Right-hand side. Very well. Could we scroll up a little bit. Up, please. It is fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we scroll down a bit, please. Further down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you need to see the Ohrid lake on the map. Yes, that's fine?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes, but if the map could somehow be magnified, please, because it's really a very small font.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we scroll it up a little bit so that we can see the border of the Republic of Macedonia. Very well now. Thank you. Could we zoom in on this part. Could we zoom out one step, please. One more step, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, is it -- is this the size of the map that is useful for you, so that you can mark the territories under the NLA control and without using that map that you now have in front of you and that you are looking at?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you think, sir, it is possible to really see the font on this map? I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark the approximate areas? I will not go into details of whether a particular village was under the control or not, but which parts of Macedonia comprised within those 20 per cent of the territory that was under the NLA control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to intervene, Mr. Apostolski, but it seems to me that if you want the witness and the Chamber to be able to read village names or even some town names and if you want the witness to be marking with any degree of reliability it will be necessary to focus in onto smaller sections of this map and go through them until gradually we complete the whole map, because the scale, at the moment, it's really not easy to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. Thank you for your suggestion, Your Honour. Could we zoom in on the part around Kumanovo now? That would be the upper part of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark in this part of the map the territory under control, and I don't want you to use your props.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, now, Mr. Apostolski, I'm going to intervene again. Are you really saying that you expect the witness to remember with any reliability to precise geographical areas covering at least 20 per cent, he says of the territory of Macedonia without any reference to any of the detail that he has with him? He would be a very impressive witness if he could do that from memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then I apologise, Your Honour, and I apologise to the witness. Maybe I went too far with my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark in this part of the map the territory that was under the NLA control at the end of the conflict in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It is going to be pretty approximate area indeed for a number of reasons. Firstly because of the scale of the map. I think this is essentially the road map of Macedonia, it's not really a military map as such. Secondly for technical reasons, I don't really think it is really physical to draw the exact line because the line which is left by this marker is at least one millimetre thick or perhaps two millimetres thick which may actually mean that this line alone will cover several kilometres on the ground. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, again, this is going to be pretty approximate area. But put in this way there was fighting in the area or perhaps there was some activities in the area Tabanovce here. Well the area of Crna Gora and east of Kumanovo was the area where there were a lot of NLA activities going on including Aracinovo and almost to Skopje, down south like this, in fact. If you could go west now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The movement we move, we lose what is there. That's why it is going to be necessary if we are to complete this process to do it view by view.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I seek to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 2D78, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move towards the left-hand side of the map, towards Tetovo. Further down, please. A bit further down, please. It's good now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark the area, the approximate area, under the NLA control in this section, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would it be more helpful for the witness to identify what he sees to be the material views on the map. That way we're likely to get, in the end, from him a more complete and reliable guide, rather than you trying to select areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you follow what I'm suggesting Mr. Bezruchenko is this a practical next area or would you like the focus of the map on the screen from what is presently being displayed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank, Your Honour, this is perfectly fine for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of Radusa as well as Zeden feature south of Radusa were apparently under NLA control. So I will again mark it pretty approximately. The area south of Tetovo-Skopje road apparently also fell under NLA control. Many of those villages fell under NLA control at the final stage of the conflict, approximately. The area west of Kumanovo experienced a lot of fighting and was under NLA control at various stages of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean to say Kumanovo or did you mean Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Tetovo, west of Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you be able, I would ask, to mark that with a number 3, the area you have just enclosed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the first area you marked with a number 1, the more northern of the remaining two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radusa and Zeden this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, and number 2, the remaining area. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you go north a little bit again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if we move, we lose.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I seek to tender this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any other area of this map before we leave it that you would want to mark.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. If you could go a little bit up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, before we move this particular view --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see what you mean. I think this area here between Gostivar and the border was more or less under NLA control, this one perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Number 4, could you mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was some NLA activities in the area of Mavrovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Number 5, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was some NLA activity in the area of Debar. I think south of Debar, but let me refer to my map again. In fact in the area of the village of Goranci, which is somewhat east of Debar, approximately here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Number 6, could I suggest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's about it, as far as this view is concerned. If you could go further up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This view will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I wanted to tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 2D79, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, just for the sake of clarity, because you comprised the road from Tetovo to Gostivar, so to clarify for the transcript, is it correct that the road from Tetovo to Gostivar was not under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Mr. Apostolski. Apparently there were some villages in the area between Tetovo and Gostivar which were indeed under NLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But to have it on record, was the road between Tetovo and Gostivar under the NLA control.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see on this map, Mr. Apostolski, there are two roads between Tetovo and Gostivar. There is the highway and there is also another road further to west. I think the village of Kamenjane and Pirok as well as Vrapciste here, if I may mark them, as well as the village of Lisec were under NLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The highway, Gostivar-Tetovo was not under the NLA control. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now scroll down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not without losing what has just been marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could I seek to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 2D80, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now which way did you want the view to be varied, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be grateful to Your Honours if the view could be moved a little bit up and left. That's enough. Can we go back actually. Okay. That's fine. Thank you. All right. Now, as I mentioned previously, many villages in this area here, in fact generally here, were under NLA control. Also, many villages in this area as well, south of this road. Approximately, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, I believe we have marked them in the previous map. I think it is the same area that you marked a while ago.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is another view. Okay. Let's go to the right, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I believe that we should go further south, because you also marked already the area around Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since in your opinion, the fronts were Kumanovo, Tetovo, Gostivar and possibly we could go south if you feel that you need to mark some area around the Ohrid lake. If you wish, I would move to the right. But Kumanovo is there, to the right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I marked the area to the left, that is to the west of Kumanovo already. I also marked the area of Zeden hill, Radusa south of Tetovo-Skopje road as well as west of Tetovo. I also marked the area in the area of Gostivar and some in the area of Debar. But we could take a look at the area of Ohrid lake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Shall we receive this, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, I don't think it needs to be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will lose this marking and move to the area south of the lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Further down a bit, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the appropriate section?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I think there was also some activities of the NLA south of Debar; here approximately. And that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honours can I seek to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 2D81, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would this be the convenient time for the break, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, Mr. Apostolski. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could the witness be shown P466, page 29 in the English version and 32 in the Macedonian version of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is paragraph 106 of your report. In your report, you used a lot of communiques, communications to the public, issued by the NLA. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you refer to them in this paragraph saying that in order to make its goals and actions known to the wider public the NLA issued a number of public communiques and in the table below, a summary of these communiques is provided as well as some addition sources.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, all these communiques were received from the Macedonian authorities through RFAs.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you received part of these communications from Ali Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall exactly. I think essentially there were three major sources for those communiques. One was the Macedonian government and as I mentioned them we receive them through official RFAs. The second one was the Macedonian Ministry of Interior "White Book" which published some of those communiques. And the third one, probably, were obtained from Mr. Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I assert to you that you received all of these communiques from Mr. Ali Ahmeti. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, sir. If you refer to the "White Book", for example, at the end of the "White Book" you will find a chapter in fact which is completely dedicated to these communiques, and I clearly remember some of those communiques translated in Macedonian. In fact, I was reading them in Macedonian, which would appear to suggest to me that they were received from Macedonian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You believed these communiques to be true.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no specific reasons to doubt the authenticity of these documents. As I said, we received many of those from Macedonian authorities, and some of them are published in the "White Book." You may wish to refer to the book and see it for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But in your report you used them -- you used them as truthful you made no comment that did you not trust these communiques.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand the implication of your question, sir. In which sense are you suggesting I should trust or not trust these communiques. Are you suggesting that they were forged or are you suggesting that they did not exist or we did not receive them?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm suggesting that some of them are fake, and I will show it to you now. If you look at the table in front of you, would you agree with me that the first column delineates the date of the communique. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The second column is the date of issue.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The third is the content of the communique.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the fourth column that provides the signature of the person that signed it.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you -- could I draw your attention to the communique dated May 5th, 2001. Do you see that -- do you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In this communique, this communique described the combat operations of the 113th Brigade in the areas of Kumanovo and Lipkovo. The communication says that the Macedonian government used Mi-24 helicopter, gun ships, a machine-gun, a 155-millimetre Howitzer, various mortars, tanks and armoured vehicles. It goes on claiming that the members of the 113th Brigade killed 20 Macedonian soldiers, police and paramilitaries, destroyed three tanks and four armoured vehicles and shot down two helicopters. Do you see that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And this communique has been signed by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You believed that this is a truthful communique.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that such communique was issued and this document does exist. However, I believe that in fact this is grossly exaggerated in a sense of [indiscernible] casualties which were suffered by the Macedonian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you never made any comment on all of this in your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, in fact, this particular section of the report deals with the public communiques issued by the NLA. I just made a summary of those communiques in tabular form. It was not my intention really to comment on each of them, and either support or deny information which is contained in those communiques. But I think it is pretty obvious from reading this communique that apparently the casualties are definitely overinflated, and you can actually see it as well in comparison with other sources. But, as I say, again, the purpose of citing this communique in my report was entirely different. I was not going to really to comment on each and every communique and say whether it was right or wrong. I just cited them as facts; that is, such communique did exist and they were actually issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you implying that the communiques given by the NLA were overexaggerated and were untruthful?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not implying that. What I'm saying is that my analysis would suggest that the information as contained in this specific communique, in terms of casualties, seems to be overinflated. But it does not necessarily mean that all the communiques were of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you believe that the NLA, in the operations in Kumanovo and Lipkovo managed to destroy three tanks, four armoured vehicles, and they shot down two helicopters.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't I don't believe it. I don't think it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you never put any comment in your report about all these notes. You never mentioned that you not believed this communiques to be truthful. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you see, sir, this entire section of the report, as I mentioned, is actually dealing with various NLA communiques. As I say, it was not really my intention to comment on this particular communique. In fact, if such comments were really justified and required to be made they would probably concern the entire operations in the area of Kumanovo and Lipkovo, not just this communique.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. So you agree with me that this communique is not a truthful one?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is exaggerated. I don't think that at any point of the conflict the Macedonian army lost two helicopters. I understand there was only one incident in which one helicopter of the Macedonian army actually crashed in the area of Popova Sapka, and there were also attempts by the NLA to shoot down Macedonian helicopters who is portable anti-aircraft missiles, but they never succeeded, at least I never saw any other reports which would confirm this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The village of Vejce is in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The village of Sipkovica is also in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And in making your report, you referred also to foreign documents.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean some --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]. .. Perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, to some international documents.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you verifying the truthfulness of these documents?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if your question implies whether I was actually evaluating the credibility of the sources and documents that they used, my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you verifying whether the content of those documents were -- was truthful?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally my analysis would not be really based on one single document but would require confirmation and substantiation derived from other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown exhibit number P466; that is page 18 in the English version and 19 in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could I draw your attention to paragraph 54 whereby you say: "The General Staff of the NLA was in Prizren while the tactical staff was in Sipkovica." And you hereby refer to footnote 68, briefing package from Macedonia. And you go on saying: "Shefi last name unknown, known as Kravata was identified as a logistics leader. Den Korabi was administrative assistant to Ali Ahmeti, Nazim Beqir was identified as the NLA spokesman, while Fazli Hajdari as operations officer and you hereby refer to footnote 69, briefing package on Macedonia. Did you verify this information mentioned in paragraph 54?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this paragraph is based not necessarily on this source alone, but also other similar sources which I reviewed throughout while preparing my report. And I tend to suggest that in fact this information in, general sense, is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me start from the beginning: "The General Staff of the NLA was located in Prizren. The tactical staff in Sipkovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the documents this was the case at least for the time being. At least for a while, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you claim that during the one period of the conflict the General Staff of the NLA was located in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ali Ahmeti would be the one who would know the best where the General Staff was located. Did you verify his statement?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to reiterate again, sir, that information which was actually contained in the statement of Mr. Ali Ahmeti was corroborated through other sources. I guess perhaps you would agree with me that sometimes those who are being interviewed have their own reasons to say and not to say certain things, and the witness statements, in many cases, seem to be quite speculative. This was the reason why I was trying to rely mostly on solid documents, including those of international organisations, specifically NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were present during the interview with Ali Ahmeti. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit number 65 ter 2D235, page 6 in both the Macedonian and the English version. That is paragraph 31. This is not the document. 65 ter 2D325.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see in front of you, this is a statement of Ali Ahmeti given on 30th of July, 2005?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could I read to you paragraph 31. Mr. Ali Ahmeti, who was the supreme military commander of the NLA in Macedonia says that the General Staff and the Supreme Command were located in Vejce in March. The Supreme Command and the General Staff moved to Sipkovica in April 2001, where it remained until the end of the conflict. Would you agree with me that Mr. Ali Ahmeti has given a statement in which he fails to mention that the General Staff was located in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. He never mentions this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And that differs from the fact that you mention.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Because what I mention is based on NATO sources, which perhaps had their own sources of information to provide. As I mentioned, I was trying to rely on my report in solid, verifiable sources. I did not find any information in the course of preparation of my report which would corroborate the fact that in March 2001, the NLA General Staff was in Vejce. Perhaps this was the fact, but I did not really find any information which would otherwise support this fact. But it is also true that the General Staff moved to Sipkovica, and I think this is adequately reflected in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The Staff was never in Prizren, as it is written in your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular information is based on NATO sources, sir, and I have no reason to doubt these sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I thank you. Is it correct that each of the NLA brigades was fighting pursuant to its own plan and assessment?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not find any evidence in the course of preparation of my report which would suggest this allegation, sir. I would suggest that in fact the actions of the NLA brigades were coordinated and in fact in broad terms were aimed towards one ultimate goal; to capture as much territory as possible, to push south along the axis along the border with Albania and gradual increase control of the areas close to the capital.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So your assertion is that the brigades had coordinated actions and coordinated plan and assessment for the actions.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently there was a general plan as to the goals to be pursued and the final resolution of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 3D367 [as interpreted]. 2D367, as the transcript is inaccurate in stating 3D.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is Gzim Ostreni's statement - do you see it in front of you - page 10 in the Macedonian version and page 11 in the English version, please, paragraph 53. Do you see the paragraph 3 in front of you. That is the statement of Gzim Ostreni. You stated that he was best able to know the information about the NLA actions as the Chief of the General Staff. Is that correct? ?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And in paragraph 53, could you see in line 6 it says: Every brigade has an area zone of responsibility and each was fighting according to its own plan and judgment. We actually did not have a chance to conduct any coordinated operation involving several brigades. Does Mr. Ali Ahmeti -- does Mr. Gezim Ostreni testify that each brigade fought in accordance with its own plan and assessment?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir, but obviously we understand this paragraph in entirely different terms. I'm afraid we're talking about different things here. What this statement says that at the tactical level each brigade indeed had its own plan; that's true. However, it also means that in a broader sense at the strategic level there was certain concepts and therefore certain coordination in the actions of these brigades. If you, again, take a look at the document titled the concept of operations and the map which you have just described, it is pretty clear, in fact that there were certain sequence of the moves an actions of the NLA brigades. Mr. Gezim Ostreni also says here that they did not have a chance to conduct any coordinated operations involving several brigades. This is absolutely right, but this is an entirely different matter. What he means here is there were no joint operations which would involve several brigades but that does not necessarily mean that there was not an overall strategic plan and the actions of the brigades was in [indiscernible] accordance with this plan were not coordinated. At least this is my understanding of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. And the section dealing the finances, section of your report, you make a summary that the NLA received large financial assistance and, among others sources of finances, you quote. But is it correct that the NLA did not create a centralised budget?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I ever use the word "budget" in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it then correct that the NLA had not created a central financial system?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, with my due respect, I don't think I used this expression as central financial system in relation to the NLA. If you're implying if there was any kind of a fund, perhaps, or if there was any system, perhaps for collecting the contributions for the NLA, I think that such fund existed and probably certain system was in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your report you make the assertion that it was an organised movement and that it was an armed conflict, that it was an uprising to attain political goals. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is an uprising process typical for democratic states where there is a possibility to resolve the problems through democratic institutions in the system?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid this is a general question which probably doesn't really relate to the subject of my report. But if you would like me to answer, I would tell that a political process to resolve the differences in social- and political-economic matters is the fundamental feature of any democratic society. Violence is not a way to resolve problems in a democratic society.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in Macedonia in 2001 the legitimate representatives were elected for the parliament and for the government?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness -- no, I will ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you say in paragraph 15 of your report that the both sides have signed the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Could you explain which two sides are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid this is a mistake which is attributable to translation. In English I think I used the word parties. This paragraph doesn't say that these parties were in fact the parties to the conflict. What I meant to say that the political parties signed the Ohrid Agreement. Of course you are aware of the fact that was indeed the case, and four major political parties in Macedonia became signatories of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the exhibit P466, page 7, both Macedonian and the English version. It is the paragraph 15, so we need to go a page back in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You say there that the most intensive period of the conflict lasted until the 13 of August 2001 when, with US and EU diplomatic intervention the -- both sides signed the Ohrid Framework Agreement although after this date, the cease-fire violations continued. Is it correct that you say in this item that both sides have signed it, or the parties signed it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to paragraph 15, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in this perhaps I referred to the political parties which signed the Ohrid Framework Agreement and these were four of these parties, if I recall, correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters wish to note that in the Macedonian version it says explicitly both sides or parties while the English version does not mention the word both.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But in paragraph 15, you did not write that it was political parties, and you say -- you say parties.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The word "political" is not there but essentially I meant political parties. And I think in fact the Ohrid Framework Agreement, as such, was not really the subject of my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you used the Ohrid Agreement as the possible end of the military conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ohrid Agreement was the document which stipulated the end of activities, of military activities and the end of violence. This document also provided fundamental changes in the constitution of Macedonia, including its preamble as well as a number of important provisions related to the use of Albanian language, educational rights in native language, proportional representation in the bodies of power, as well as rearrangement of certain functions and administrative powers at the municipal level. So if you would really like me to comment more on that agreement I could probably tell you more. But as I say it was not really the primary objective of my analysis.
