I think we actually can regard this agreement as the fundamental document which diplomatically and formally put an end to violence, but I think the real end of the conflict could have occurred on 26th September 2001 when the NLA declared that it was formally demobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you say that it was demobilised, does it mean that it was disarmed?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "demobilised," I mean that it was declared that it was demobilised, and this happened after the end of Operation Essential Harvest.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does mean that it was disarmed as well?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA surrendered a certain amount of weapons which apparently was previously agreed under the terms of the arrangement which involved Macedonian authorities, the NLA, and NATO. If your question implies whether there was any weapons which reportedly would have been left in NLA's disposal, at NLA's disposal, I simply cannot answer this question because I was not really looking to this aspect as the final date which was in fact a benchmark for me in relation to the duration of the conflict, which was 26th September 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would ask to you answer me briefly. In your opinion, and from the review of the documents that you did when preparing this report, the NLA was disarmed at the 26th of September.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the NLA statement said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that the assertion that you make as well?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that the cease-fire violations actually continued after a while, and perhaps the real process of demobilisation was quite difficult, but it is very difficult to establish in fact which particular units were immediately demobilised and for which it took sometime to get demobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the 113th Brigade return all the weapons?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell that, sir, because I was not really involved in this operation, and I didn't see any documents which would suggest that they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Ljuboten was under the competence of the 113th Brigade [as interpreted]. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. Actually, it was 114th Brigade which was operating in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise there is a mistake in the transcript I asked whether it was correct that Ljuboten was an area controlled by the 114th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you gave your answer already. Could you tell me whether the 114th Brigade was disarmed on the 26th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that all the NLA brigades surrendered a number of weapons which, in totality, amounted to the numbers which were agreed upon previously. But if your question specifically refers to 114th Brigade, I cannot really give you a definitive answer, because -- for a number of reasons. Firstly, I did not see the exact list of weapons that was in the possession of this brigade. And, secondly, I did not see any documents that would suggest that the amount that this brigade actually had was above the amount which was surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you now agree with me that in your report there is a separate section that deals with the events of Ljuboten, 10 to 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The Prosecutor's office has requested from you to review the relevant documents and materials and to express your opinion about the actions of the Macedonian forces in the village of Ljuboten on the 11th and the 12th of August, 2001. Also, the analysis of these events was based on three sources as well: Macedonian security forces that comprised both the army and the police; the NLA sources; and international sources. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you visited the area in and around Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had, I think, two brief visits.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you visit the positions of the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm referring to the positions of the Macedonian security forces as they were in August 2001, 10 to 12 August.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I visited the positions of the Macedonian army above the village of Ljuboten, and I found some old trenches and apparently mortar positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you visit the position Smok?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you at Ljubotenski Bacila, where, on August 10, 2001, Macedonian soldiers were killed and wounded?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you visit Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We just passed through this village on our way to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you notice any football stadium or field when -- on the road when you were going from Ljubanci to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that this football field was really the focus of my attention. I was more interested in the positions of the Macedonian army, especially mortar and artillery positions, above the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you visit the location where the Radisani police check-point was located?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we went to Radisani; at least I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you used witness statements? I'm asking you about foreigners, Henry Bolton, as well as the personal notes of Franz-Josef Hutsch, the Prosecution witness?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously I was trying as much as possible not to use any witness statements in my report at all. If there were such instances, they were very rare and only for illustration of very specific points.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As international sources you used the Human Rights Watch report as well as the personal notes of Franz-Josef Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you had access to all the written documents in OTP's possession in respect to the Ljuboten events or from between 10th and 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you review all the documents related to the events in Ljuboten in 2001 coming from the international sources?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, as you would imagine, in fact my report has probably over 1.000, even more, footnotes, so the number of documents which I used is really quite significant. I'm afraid that if I tell you that I have seen every document, I might actually make an error, because it would be simply impossible for me to claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you aware with the OSCE reports about the events in Ljuboten? Did you review that report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which specific report do you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The report of 16th of August, 2001. That is a special report on the Ljuboten incident.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were some reports to this extent. Can I specifically be shown this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will now show it to you to refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown exhibit number 1D24.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have access to this document while preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the next page, please. I think I have seen this report, but I'm afraid that I have seen this report after actually my report was completed, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that you were following the trial since its beginning.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Didn't you consider this document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Didn't you think that this document deserved bigger attention in respect to the Ljuboten events of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, my report was completed, as you may imagine, before the trial started. Now, this is the OSCE document --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But once you made your draft report, your preliminary report, you amended it later.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Let me finish, sir, please. As I said, this is the OSCE report. The OSCE, of course, had their own monitors on the ground. But having said that I would rather rely on the reports that were produced by the Macedonian army and the Macedonian Ministry of Defence which seem to be quite more reliable in terms of the actual facts and details relating to the events in Ljuboten for one simple reason they actually originated from the primary sources. This report describes events post-factum. This is dated after, actually -- after actual events in Ljuboten, and this report seems to be somewhat speculative, in a sense that it provides its assessments. But having said that, I wouldn't say that this is an incorrect report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you used the report of human rights watch report which was entitled: Abuse against civilians --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters apologise, they didn't get the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think at the very beginning of my work on my report there is one of the documents that we really had at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is a post-factual document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you, nevertheless, [Realtime transcript read in error "never"] paid attention to it and you quoted it in your report about the attacks in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I specifically quote this report in the part of my report which deals with the attack on Ljuboten. If I do it's probably, actually we have to verify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise I was misinterpreted in line 19. "Never paid attention" should read "you paid attention."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the report of the Human Rights Watch group?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to the Human Rights Watch report. And you quote them in your summary related to the Ljuboten attacks, and you refer to them in paragraph 483 of your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you thereby say that the OSCE observers in the Human Rights Watch report investigators that visited the village -- I apologise. There is the mistake in the Macedonian translation that I read. The investigators of Human Rights Watch who visited the village immediately after the attack found no trenches, no bunkers, no machine-gun posts, no sandbags post that would present evidence for an organised presence of the NLA units in defence preparations. Is it correct that based on the report of Human Rights Watch, you came to such a conclusion in your resume?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, I do quote this report in my report, but I also quote other documents which seem be to at variance with this particular report and these documents were quoted in the amendment which I prepared at a later stage. I would probably like to draw your attention specifically to paragraph 481 (A) of my report, and can I read this paragraph to you. "According to ministry" --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will allow it -- I will allow you to read it but you do not refer to it in your summary about the Ljuboten attacks between 10th and 12th of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the documents which we have received actually were received after my report was completed. The addendum is based on entirely new documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Although you amended your initial report, you felt no need to make yet another addendum that would present the factual situation regarding the Ljuboten events between the 10th and 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, if you really read carefully the amended addendum to my report, you will probably see that out of about perhaps 20 paragraphs well, three quarter of those paragraph s are actually related to the events in Ljuboten. And let me read there paragraph to you again. This is paragraph 418 (A): "According to Ministry of Interior documents as early as February and March 2001, the administration for security and counter-intelligence was receiving indications that the NLA was recruiting fighters in Ljuboten. In June 2001, information was received that NLA was planning to establish a corridor between Aracinovo and Ljuboten to facilitate NLA actions towards Skopje and to provide logistics for NLA forces in Aracinovo. Bunkers were reportedly prepared in Ljuboten by end of June 2001."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page -- the fifth English -- the fifth English page and pages 4 and 5 of the document that is now displayed. This is the OSCE special report on the Ljuboten incident dated 16th of August, 2001. The part starting with: "Finally it appears highly likely that there were EAAG in the village during the recent hostilities and that the EAAG have influence in the village. In this context, the Human Dimension Officer of the mission finds reports that the ethnic Albanian villages remained in their homes during the hostilities 'because they are loyal citizens who had no reason to leave' profoundly disturbing. The mission is unaware of a village free of EAAG influence in which the majority of the ethnic Albanian population made the decision to remain in their homes with their families when an armed conflict was erupting in the village or nearby. It only happens in villages with an EAAG presence." EAAG is an abbreviation of OSCE for the NLA. It uses it in its report. May I read onward: "There does appear to be an EAAG tactic involving the use of, at the very lest' suggestions' and informal pressure on villagers to remain during fighting. This tactic effectively results in the use of civilians as human shields. It also leaves them exposed to incidents with troops. It is intended to produce either government inaction in the face of aggression or incidents that can be exploited for propaganda. It is thus not only illegal but a cynical abuse of a friendly vulnerable local population by armed groups." Mr. Bezruchenko, didn't you think that this OSCE report would be useful to refer to in preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say the following: These two paragraphs which you have just quoted in fact do not really say anything new to me. There were numerous allegation in media and many other documents that in fact the NLA was pressuring the local population to stay in the village in terms of combat activities. So I don't really find any particular value in these two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You put -- are you claiming that the media report and the OSCE reports have the same value?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What -- what I'm saying is that there were lots of reports which I have seen including similar reports from OSCE as well and other international agencies, media reports, statements by various political and governmental figures, to the extend that, indeed, the NLA was pressuring villagers in some of those villages to stay and essentially hold them as human shields. But I think we have discussed this issue already previously, and I think I mention already that the plight of civilian population and the problems regarding the safety of villagers were reflected in those reports which I quote in the section 5 of my report dealing with chronology of the conflict. Well, I don't really see any particular value, again to reiterate this point, because it was highly known at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you failed to mention this in the chapter where you speak about the NLA tactics. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two paragraphs seem to describe a very generic terms the situation despite the fact that the whole report really deals with Ljuboten. This report will also contradict the statements of some of the villagers, residents in the village of Ljuboten. Therefore, it would be very difficult for me to rely on this report only in assessing whether the villagers of Ljuboten were indeed forced to stay or not. But I think I have seen at least one report, Macedonian military report, which suggested that they were indeed pressured.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. We will continue now. Were you aware of the reports of the German embassy related to the events in Ljuboten in the period between 10th and 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which specific report you are referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you like to have it displayed on the monitor so you can refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 1D224. Could we see the English version? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you aware of this document when you were preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think by the time I prepared my report, we did not already receive this document, but I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you of the opinion that this document might be useful for the preparation of your report or for the amended part of your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably not really very much useful, because as I mentioned previously, in the section of the report specifically dealing with Ljuboten I found much better sources from Macedonian military intelligence and the directorate for security and counter-intelligence than any other reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If you are able to see, this is subject information on Ljuboten. Do you see that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You can see below description of the events, under 2.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please scroll down just little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay, this is good. I would read the account of events as described by the German embassy about the Ljuboten events in the period 10 to 12th of August 2001: "Intensive conversations have yielded the following course of events. Ljuboten was a majority population of Albanian ethnicity and one part of it is inhabit the by Macedonians. The mine incident of 10th of August happened on one of the approaches to the Albanian part of the town. The NLA, National Liberation Army, tried to capture the town in several hit-and-run attempts but was prevented from doing so by the Macedonian security forces. "The attack by the security forces of 12 August was led by the Macedonian part of the town against the centre of the town. There is no doubt that the first three mortar attacks were aimed at the security forces. It was the Macedonian forces which then followed by using further mortars." Would you agree with me that the German embassy, as an independent source of information, was an independent source of information because it was neither on the Macedonian nor on the Albanian side and that it presents an accurate description of the events and that it would be useful to use this document in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously, sir, I think that my report was completed by the time we received this document. This is first point I would like to make. Second point that I would like to make is that what this document says, especially in the first -- in paragraph 2, is not really corroborated by other sources, specifically Macedonian sources. Point three which I would like to make about this report, it seems to be based on a number of interviews which apparently was made with some Macedonian military personnel, as it says intensive conversation have yielded the following course of events. I did not see any Macedonian military reports which would suggest that the NLA was trying to capture Ljuboten prior to the date of 12 August 2001, especially in what is described as hit-and-run attempts. I actually went through all the Macedonian military reports, General Staff reports, I mean operational reports, through the month of August, and there is nothing to suggest that any such actions actually took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding as --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise you can finish your testimony. I thought you were done.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the mortar attacks which were in the security forces, there was indeed some mortar exchange around the village. However, to suggest that the first three mortar attacks were aimed at the security forces does not really get any confirmation from the Macedonian military reports. I think what happened is that on this particular date, on 12 of August, in fact NLA attacked Macedonian army positions quite late. This was on the second -- on the 12th of August. At least this is evident from the record of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is this a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We adjourn now and will resume at 1.00, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, you finalised your first report on the 30th of March, 2006. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The Defence received that batch -- I apologise. The Defence received your report on the 31st of March, 2006. It was the batch 17. When producing your first report, you had access to all documents of the OTP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You will access to documents in the Macedonian, the B/C/S, the English language, and since you said yourself you speak all those languages, you did not need to wait for the translation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Otherwise I'm afraid the whole process might have been delayed for a very long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated today that the OSCE report was not accessible to you before you produced your first report. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I put it in a slightly different way. I think I said that I saw this report perhaps after my report was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If I tell that you the Defence received this report from the OTP on the 7th of November, 2005, in the batch 3, that means that you have had access to that document before producing your first report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that may be correct, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So do you agree with me that you have had access to this document, even before producing your first report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have to repeat my previous answer, sir. I think that I saw this report after my report was actually done.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember that I showed you also the document from the German embassy related to the events in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember saying that you had not seen this document before you had produced your first report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not really say that. I think I said that, I think I saw this report, well, after my report had been done. But, again, I'm not sure. But just to comment on this, I don't really think that either of these report are of significantly particular value for my report for the reasons which I have already explained. There are dozens and dozens of similar documents which have been analysed and which seem to totally fitting into the general picture as described in my report, and they are of far better quality than these two reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You had an opportunity to get acquainted with the statement of Peter Matthiesen, the military attache to Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I read his statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If I tell that you Peter Matthiesen in the second statement of 16th and 18th January, 2006 enclosed also the document I showed, do you agree with me that this report had been available to you before you had produced your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a number of documents that Mr. Matthiesen provided for the Office of the Prosecutor, perhaps including this particular report, but in fact, as I mentioned previously, essential aspects of my report were already pretty well covered by the Macedonian military documents, especially those of military intelligence and the directorate for security and counter-intelligence of the Ministry of Interior. So if there were any documents of value at all provided by Mr. Matthiesen, they were very, very few and as compared to the other documents provided by original sources, that is the Macedonian military, they would be perhaps of secondary value for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So your statement given before this Court that you had not seen these documents before producing your first report is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not, it's not. I think I indeed saw these documents after my report was produced, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But as a military analyst, you should have reviewed all documents.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I was doing; that's right. I, indeed, reviewed all documents and selected those which I found best.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You had submitted your amended report in August 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this report is not essentially different from your first report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is not essential different, but I think, actually, the amended addendum contains several valuable pieces of information which might perhaps help you to rearrange certain accents related to the events in Macedonia in 2001 and those related to Ljuboten as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In this second report of yours, you're not quoting witness statements. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, sir, and I don't really know how many times I have already been repeating this throughout my testimony, that I was trying to rely mainly on the solid verifiable and reliable documents, trying to remove any witness statements of speculative nature as much as it possibly could be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From the footnotes, you removed all references to witness statements and to investigator's notes from the witness interviews. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If I tell you that in the footnotes you quote from witness statements for at least 180 times, that fact would be correct? I'm now speaking about the first report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a somewhat overinflated number, but I think there was indeed quite a big number of witness statements which I quoted in my report, original report, for the lack of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that your original, your first report, was based on the witness statements, statements of the witnesses for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only partly. As I say, from the very beginning, I was trying to really build my report on the basis of documents, but inevitably in the course of the writing of reports, I identified a number of gaps which somehow had to be addressed in any case for the sake of making the report address all appropriate issues and aspects. In such situations, whenever there were simply no documents to provide any information about certain issue or a point which could be, at times, pretty subtle but important, I inevitably had to rely on witness statements. But, again, I must say, that even at that stage, at the very beginning, while working on my report back in 2006, I was really trying to minimise the number of such witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that in the part of the report dealing with Ljuboten, you are referring to notes and sketches drawn by the witness Franz-Josef Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Unfortunately, or due to certain circumstances, I had no other way, as not to rely on some of the documents provided by Mr. Franz-Josef Hutsch, because there were some points related to the events in Ljuboten which really presented significant gaps in what I was trying to present. Therefore, it appeared to me that those documents presented by Franz-Josef Hutsch would be useful documents to specifically address these points. I would like to emphasise again, that unfortunately, there were no other documents to fill in these gaps, but if I didn't do it, I would feel that my report would actually have been incomplete without addressing these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you, as a military analyst, were present during the interviews of all military questioned -- regarding their presence at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I mentioned already in the course of this testimony that I was present at some interviews. I'm not really entirely sure if I was present at all interviews of military personnel. I think not. I wasn't present at some of those?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will go back to a question related to the witness Franz-Josef Hutsch and his sketches. Is it correct that when you are quoting from him in your report, you are saying that he was a former German military officer?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say and would it be included in the report that he was a German journalist during the time when he was present at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That perhaps would make certain sense, but for me the fact that he was a former German military officer with apparently military training and background as well as some experience would be far more important, because his opinion would present some professional military matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And, for instance, Peter Matthiesen, as a military attache, did it not seem a more credible source regarding the reports?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is a significant difference between the statement of Mr. Matthiesen and Mr. Hutsch, because I don't think Mr. Matthiesen ever claimed that he was in the area of Ljuboten in the period which I described in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But, surely, as a military attache, he would not provide an untruthful report. He would surely base it on ascertained facts.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have no reasons to doubt the truthfulness of the report of Mr. Matthiesen, but let me explain again. When dealing with this specific section related to the events in Ljuboten, I inevitably had to rely on some documents presented by Mr. Hutsch who claimed to be there in the area; and in fact, I did not really have any reasons, serious reasons, to doubt that he had not been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Inter alia, you refer to a sketch admitted in evidence by this Chamber, P00296, whereby he drawed the village of Ljubanci and explains the situation on 11th of August, 2001. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was such a sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you verify the sketch with the actual situation on the terrain? Is it corresponding to the situation in the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you actually mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is the sketch in correspondence with the map of the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say, I have not really seen such a thing as the map of village of Ljubanci, and I don't think we ever received such a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On that map, on that sketch prepared by Franz-Josef Hutsch, you refer to it in footnote 668 and you quote it in paragraph 507. The entire paragraph 507 is based on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would appear so. Unfortunately, I did not see any other documents which would actually support this paragraph. Support or deny this paragraph, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you considered it truthful and, for that reason, you quoted it in paragraph 507 of your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, at the time of the writing of this report, I didn't really have any reasons to doubt what Mr. Hutsch said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you did not verify it.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand, sir, how would you expect me to verify any specific point of Mr. Hutsch's report? Did you expect me to go on the ground to Ljuboten to actually make a comparison between his sketch and the location of the houses in the village? I mean, what do you exactly mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Exactly what I had in mind. Wouldn't it be necessary to go at the spot and verify all the allegations and then to proceed in writing your report. As you said previously, you were at the location, you verified the location of the Macedonian security forces. You were at the Smok position you were at the Bumbar [phoen] position, you were at the Ljubotenski Bacila. Didn't you feel it necessary to verify the other things as well?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was verifying the information which we received through a number of sources, including the reports of the Macedonian military and police, as well as some witness statements. I think that this verification was, in fact, aimed to avoid any significant mistakes in my assessment of that situation. I am not certain if -- at least I am still not certain if the sketches which were provided by Mr. Hutsch contained any significant mistakes or discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As a further source of information to compose your report regarding the events in Ljuboten in August 2001, between 10th and 12th of August, you refer to the sources coming from the NLA as well.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you only used one NLA document as a source?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which particular document do you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Document quoted in footnote 699, a NLA document, the document of the National Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I quoted this document in footnote 699.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Entire paragraph 526 is -- in the entire paragraph 526 you refer to the NLA document in that paragraph about a person called Muzafer Agushi. It is said that his -- with -- coming from Aracinovo was called on 12th of August in or in the vicinity of the village of Ljuboten. Could you tell me whether -- since you are mentioning two occasions here could you tell me whether he was killed inside or in the vicinity of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document which I quote, and I could probably tell you the 65 ter number - this is 65 ter 778 - does not really specify exactly where this person was killed. In fact, this document contains a number of columns describing the names of the persons, the date of birth, the location of birth, the location of death, the date of death, and the location of burial. In the column, the location of death is just indicated Ljuboten for this very person.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the column contains the word "Ljuboten," as you quote it as the place where this NLA member was killed. It doesn't mention the vicinity of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So it would be correct in paragraph 526 to read when referring to that document that the NLA fighter Muzafer Agushi born on 20th of July 1981, born in Aracinovo was killed on 12th of August, 2001 in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose this is also the way you could also read this document, but it would be also perhaps reasonable to suggest that this person could also be killed in the vicinity of Ljuboten, as we know that a lot of fighting was taking place on this date around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Preparing your report on the Ljuboten events in 2001, you further on -- you were also using the so-called Macedonian sources.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are, indeed, Macedonian sources, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: These are sources from -- these are written documents of the Macedonian security forces and that are the military and the police.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could I draw your attention to the footnote 675. That is a consolidated statement of the witness Osman Ramadani pursuant to Rule 92 ter. This is a statement of Osman Ramadani pursuant to Rule 92 ter, paragraphs 12 and 15. Could you explain what group would you put these statements in?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, apparently this is the statement of a resident of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But in the beginning your sources, you group in sources coming from the NLA, international sources as well as Macedonian sources. Would that mean that these two -- what group of sources would you put these statements into?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't really ascribe this statement to any particular group, but when I was describing the three groups of sources, I broadly meant that in fact each of those groups also included the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And how would you group these witnesses, what would group would you put him into?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't really regard him really as a NLA source because I don't have any evidence, real evidence that this particular individual belonged to the NLA. Well, perhaps I could just regard this particular statement little bit as a -- as a stand-alone document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: A third source of information used by you for the Ljuboten events in 2001 between the dates 10th to 12th August you mentioned the Macedonian sources. As you said -- is it correct you said you were present during the interview of several military personnel. Did you include these interviews in the group of sources of Macedonian sources?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I will rephrase it. You were present during the interview of Captain Nikolce Grozdanov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that correct that during the interview, Mr. Nikolce Grozdanov have marked photographs about the NLA positions in the village of Ljuboten on 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I would say that he actually marked several targets which his unit targeted in the village of Ljuboten. And I believe he also assumed that these targets belonged to the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you think it useful to use this photograph as an evidence received from the Macedonian side in the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall which specific photograph you mean, sir, but if you are referring to various reports by the Macedonian military regarding specific targets in Ljuboten, they were indeed a very thorough subject of my scrutiny through the preparation of my report. There was a number of reports which were made by the Macedonian military men, officers of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade, as well as officers belonging to the headquarters of the 1st Guardist Brigade which I analysed in the course of preparation of my report, including the reports provided by, for instance, Lieutenant Mario Jurisic, Captain Grozdanovski, Lieutenant Brasnarski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Your Honours I know this is a bit earlier but could we adjourn now? I will go on to a different group of questions, and I would like to inform the Chamber and my learned colleague from the Prosecution that is my intention to finish during the first session of the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Apostolski. We will adjourn now. We resume on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
